query: A TiVNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy has been reported in a single-phase BCC, dendritic state, with a yield strength of about 800 MPa and roughly 40% strain under lower-temperature testing, but at 1273 K it retains only 330 MPa yield strength and 423 MPa compressive strength at 30% strain. For its use as an intermediate layer that transfers heat between W and CuCrZr while preserving structural integrity, what single intervention could overcome this loss of strength at elevated temperature? State the proposed intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the reported baseline, define the applicable thermal and mechanical boundary conditions, identify supporting prior evidence, and propose a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small interstitial carbon content (~0.3 at.% C) to the single-phase BCC TiVNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy and then homogenizing at 1473 K will precipitate a fine, thermally stable dispersion of (Ti,Nb,Ta)C carbides that remain stable to at least 1273 K, thereby increasing the 1273 K compressive yield strength by ≥50 % (to >500 MPa) relative to the undoped alloy while retaining ≥25 % compressive plastic strain.
generation.material_initial_state: Arc-melted TiVNbTa high-entropy alloy in a single-phase BCC, dendritic microstructure; baseline properties: ~800 MPa yield strength and ~40 % strain at 298 K; ~330 MPa compressive yield strength and ~30 % strain at 1273 K.
generation.intervention: Introduce 0.3 at.% carbon during powder blending prior to arc melting, followed by a 24 h homogenization heat treatment at 1473 K under high vacuum/Ar to promote uniform distribution and controlled precipitation of nano-scale MC-type (Ti,Nb,Ta)C particles.
generation.conditions: Mechanical loading in compression or tension at 298–1273 K, strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹, in high-vacuum or He gas environment relevant to fusion heat-transfer layers.
generation.structural_mediator: ≈5–20 nm MC-type carbides [(Ti,Nb,Ta)C] coherent or semi-coherent with the BCC matrix and pinned at grain boundaries and within grains.
generation.mechanism: 1) Orowan bypass strengthening from nanoscale carbides impeding dislocation motion, which is retained at high T because of the carbides’ high melting point and low coarsening rate; 2) Zener pinning of grain boundaries retards grain growth at 1273 K, maintaining a fine BCC matrix that contributes Hall-Petch strengthening.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compressive yield strength at 1273 K rises from 330 ± 20 MPa (baseline) to ≥500 MPa, and 30 % true strain strength from 423 MPa to ≥600 MPa; room-temperature yield strength increases modestly (≤15 %). Ductility at 1273 K remains ≥25 % true strain.
generation.baseline: TiVNbTa without carbon: σy(1273 K) ≈ 330 MPa; σ30%(1273 K) ≈ 423 MPa; ε_f(1273 K) ≈ 30 %.
generation.boundary: Effect persists up to ~1400 K; above this temperature carbide coarsening reduces strengthening. Carbon additions >1 at.% risk forming continuous grain-boundary films that embrittle the alloy at 298 K.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of strengthening depends on achieving a uniform, nanoscale carbide dispersion; insufficient homogenization or excessive coarsening could negate the benefit. Possible trade-off with room-temperature ductility is uncertain without experiment.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two alloys: (i) baseline TiVNbTa and (ii) TiVNbTa-0.3 at.% C. Apply identical arc melting, hot isostatic pressing, and 1473 K/24 h homogenization. Machine cylindrical compression samples (ϕ = 3 mm, h = 4.5 mm). Perform compression tests at 298 K and 1273 K (10⁻³ s⁻¹). Characterize precipitates and grain size via TEM and EBSD before and after testing.
measurements: Compressive yield strength (0.2 % offset) at 298 K and 1273 K
True stress at 30 % strain at 1273 K
Carbide size distribution and volume fraction
Grain size after heat treatment and post-deformation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if either (a) σy at 1273 K for the C-doped alloy is <25 % higher than baseline (i.e., <413 MPa) or (b) TEM shows no stable nanoscale carbides (<30 nm) after 1273 K exposure for 1 h.
